title: Collatz Conjecture: Does Every Positive Integer Reach 1

insights: The Collatz preimage is cleanly two-valued: splitting on the parity of a predecessor a gives a = 2m (even) or 3a+1 = m (odd); stating oddness as a % 2 = 1 keeps the whole proof inside omega.
Odd predecessors are governed by a single residue: an odd a = 2t+1 gives 3a+1 = 6t+4, so odd predecessors of m exist exactly when m ≡ 4 (mod 6), and the unique odd predecessor is 2*(m/6)+1.
In-degree dichotomy: every m has the even predecessor 2m, so vertices with m ≡ 4 (mod 6) have in-degree 2 and all others in-degree 1 — one residue in six branches.
Backward closure (collatz a = m, m reaches 1 ⟹ a reaches 1) makes the basin of 1 exactly the set generated from 1 by the set-valued predecessor map — the Collatz tree rooted at 1.
Infinitude of the basin is unconditional and elementary (powers of two), far weaker than the conjecture; it cleanly separates a provable sub-statement from the open problem.

The in-degree-2 (branching) vertices of the Collatz graph are exactly the arithmetic progression 6j+4; enumerating them injectively gives an EXACT count — precisely k below 6k — so branch vertices have density exactly 1/6. This realizes the nextStep 'verified density result' in clean closed form, unconditionally.

omega does not beta-reduce a Set.range/Finset.image enumeration lambda left in the goal or hypothesis (↑((fun j => 6*j+4) x) stays opaque); coerce with show / a typed have (h : 6*a+4 = 6*b+4 := hab) before calling omega. Finset.mem_image-introduced existentials ARE beta-reduced by simp, but Set.mem_range ones are not.

The in-degree-≤2 dichotomy upgrades to a geometric tree-size bound by covering each predecessor set with the FIXED pair {2m,(m-1)/3} (an over-approximation that is a genuine Finset, so it sums cleanly via Finset.card_biUnion_le). The Set-level step bound is recovered from the Finset one through Set.Finite.toFinset + coe_toFinset; the iteration uses collatz^[d+1]=collatz^[d]∘collatz (Function.iterate_succ, NOT iterate_succ') so that one more collatz preimage is peeled at the OUTSIDE, matching collatz⁻¹'(d-step set).
nextSteps: Lower-bound companion: the backward tree also grows at least linearly — every vertex has the even predecessor 2m, so |collatz^[d]⁻¹'{m}| ≥ 1 with equality iff no ancestor in d levels is ≡4 mod6; characterize when the 2^d bound is tight (a full level of branch vertices).

Density refinement: combine ancestors_ncard_le (≤2^d) with branch_count (density 1/6 of branch vertices) toward a sharper growth rate than the crude 2^d — expected branching factor is ~(1 + 1/6) per generic level, suggesting |d-step ancestors| ~ (7/6)^d heuristically.

Connect to cycle exclusion (collatz-cycles family): a verified acyclicity statement for the basin minus {1,4,2} would let the backward tree from 1 be counted without overlap, turning the ≤2^d node bound into a genuine count of distinct numbers reaching 1 within d steps.
Two-step predecessor structure in closed residue-class form by iterating collatz_eq_iff (count of 2-step predecessors ranges 1..4 by mod-cases).
